# A reflected-ball buffer gives exact three-fiber depth
simplex-specific directional profile. The following proof retains
actual fibers and every ambient halfspace. It is a scoped construction
lemma, not an OC reduction.

## 1. Exact hypotheses and conclusion

Let d>=1. Let K,A,R be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in R^d,
and assume

    (A+R)/2 subset K.

Translate coordinates so that zero is an ordinary deepest point of K.
Write q for its maximum raw ordinary halfspace depth and a=|A|>0.
Assume there are v in R^d and 0<=delta<r such that

    A subset B(v,delta),
    B(-v,r) subset R,
    a <= beta_d(r,delta),                              (1)

where beta_d(r,delta) is the volume of the Euclidean ball cap

    {x in B(0,r): u dot x>=delta}

for any unit vector u. Its value is independent of u and is exactly

    beta_d(r,delta)
      =kappa_(d-1) integral_delta^r
                       (r^2-s^2)^((d-1)/2) ds,          (2)

with kappa_0=1. Any rigorously proved lower bound on this cap volume
can replace the right side in (1).

Let C be the convex hull of A,K,R lifted to bases -1,0,1, and measure
S=C intersect (Z times R^d) by mixed d-volume. Its actual integer
fibers are precisely A,K,R. Then

    max_(x in K) raw_depth_S(0,x)=q+a,
    raw_depth_S(0,0)=q+a,
    max_(y in S) raw_depth_S(y)=max(q+a,D(R)),           (3)

where D(R) is the maximum raw ordinary depth of R.

In particular, if R is centrally symmetric and |R|=2(q+a), its
center at base1 is also a global deepest point, and the global
maximum is exactly q+a. No formula for q is assumed.

## 2. Attainment and physical fibers

For completeness, q is an attained positive number. For unit u and
x in K, the through-x cap volume is continuous jointly in (u,x),
by dominated convergence and the nullity of hyperplanes for ordinary
d-volume. Moving any containing cap to pass through x shows that
ordinary depth is its minimum over the compact unit sphere. It is
therefore continuous on K and attains a maximum. An interior ball
supplies a point of positive depth, while a supporting outward cap
gives depth zero at every boundary point. A deepest point may thus
be translated to zero in int K. Opposite cap volumes sum to |K|,
so q<=|K|/2.

The extreme base sections of C are A and R. At base zero, any lifted
convex combination has equal weights on A and R, and is a convex
combination of K with (A+R)/2. The compatibility assumption makes
this section exactly K. The projection is [-1,1], so these are the
only integer fibers. The body is full-dimensional and all three
fibers have positive d-volume.

## 3. Uniform all-halfspace buffer estimate

Move a containing ambient cap at (0,0) parallel to itself to pass
through that point. For a nonzero continuous normal, normalize it
to unit u and write the cap as

    u dot x+b z>=0.

Its middle contribution is at least q. If it contains all of A at
base -1, it contributes another a. Otherwise choose x_A in A with
u dot x_A<b. Since A subset B(v,delta), this implies

    b>u dot v-delta.

Every point x in B(-v,r) satisfying u dot (x+v)>=delta therefore
has u dot x+b>0 and lies in the right cap. The right contribution
is at least beta_d(r,delta)>=a. Thus every nonvertical cap has
mass at least q+a, using one actual shared integer coefficient b.

A purely integer closed through-point cap contains all of K and
at least one endpoint. Condition (1) implies |R|>=a because R
contains the buffer cap. Consequently its mass is at least |K|+a,
which is at least q+a. This argument retains the entire boundary
fiber. It proves the lower bound at the single actual point (0,0).

## 4. Exact upper bounds and critical-cap inheritance

For any x in K and any own cap containing it, a sufficiently large
negative integer tilt keeps its middle trace, captures all of A,
and excludes R. Hence mixed depth at (0,x) is at most its ordinary
depth in K plus a, and in particular at most q+a. This proves the
first two assertions of (3).

At an exposed endpoint base, sufficiently large finite integer tilts
isolate any own cap from the other two bounded fibers. Its mixed
depth is therefore exactly its ordinary depth. Since D(A)<=a<q+a,
the global formula in (3) follows. For a centrally symmetric R,
its center has ordinary depth |R|/2 by symmetry, and opposite
through-point caps bound every point's depth by that same number.
This proves the stated two-contact specialization.

Every ordinary critical cap of K at zero becomes a global critical
cap after such isolation whenever D(R)<=q+a. If a finite collection
of those ordinary critical normals positively balances, choose one
common sufficiently large negative integer tilt. Their ambient
margins have nonnegative weighted sum at every z<=0, so they cover
every continuous plane over that half-line. When R is symmetric
with |R|/2=q+a, an isolated opposite pair at its center covers every
plane over z>=1. Thus a critical triple of K produces a genuine
three-plus-two global cover, with all five masses exactly q+a.

This last statement assumes the indicated ordinary critical triple;
it does not silently classify the critical menu of an arbitrary K.
It also makes no claim that a subsequent sampled fold is convex.
The independent exact planar construction in
`candidate fc66a0bec6505bfb`
uses an elementary rectangle lower bound for (2) and exhibits the
opposite behavior for its folded Ball body.
